page_metadata.title: Development of PBPK Models for PFOA and PFOS for Human Pregnancy and Lactation Life Stages

model_classification.evidence_quote: Physiologically-based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) models were developed for PFOA & PFOS for the gestation and lactation life stages in humans.

model_context.model_origin: adapted from previously developed adult human and rat PFOA/PFOS PBPK models and extended for pregnancy and lactation
model_context.stated_purpose: Represent maternal, fetal and infant kinetics of PFOA/PFOS across gestation and lactation and estimate maternal exposure
model_context.dose_metric: maternal/fetal/infant plasma or serum and milk concentrations; maternal exposure estimates

adme_determinants: life-stage-dependent maternal body weight and tissue volumes
maternal and fetal cardiac output and blood flows
renal filtration and saturable renal resorption

stated_assumptions.description: Only free chemical partitions into tissues; explicit plasma protein binding is not simulated.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: Only the free concentration of chemical partitions into tissues... explicit binding of PFAAs to plasma proteins is not simulated.

stated_assumptions.description: Placental transfer is treated as simple bidirectional diffusion; active transport is not modeled.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: Placental transfer simple diffusion bidirectional; possible active transport not modeled.

stated_assumptions.description: The lactation model has no explicit mammary tissue compartment and places plasma chemical in direct contact with milk.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: A mammary compartment is not explicitly represented... Chemical in plasma was placed in direct contact with the milk compartment.

stated_assumptions.description: The infant is represented as a single compartment because of limited data.
stated_assumptions.evidence_quote: the infant part of the model was treated as a single compartment with a volume of distribution.

connections.evidence: Adult human PFAA uptake model retained
Fetal tissues are lumped into rest of body

absorption.evidence_quote: The pregnancy model retained adult-model uptake pathways; the lactation model similarly uses the adult human PFAA model.

elimination.evidence_quote: Maternal clearance is urinary; infant clearance is first-order.

unresolved.description: Pregnancy and lactation use different structures.
unresolved.reason: Pregnancy has placenta/fetus/amniotic fluid and an explicit mammary tissue compartment; lactation directly links maternal plasma to milk and uses a single infant compartment.

allometric_scaling_rules: Urinary elimination rate constants scaled as BW^-0.25
Fetal plasma volume is a constant fraction of fetal body weight
Adult maternal chemical parameters retained; placental, milk and infant parameters calibrated separately

connections.evidence: Adult human PFAA uptake model retained
Fetal tissues are lumped into rest of body
Plasma chemical directly contacts milk; milk:plasma partition and mammary blood flow are used
Milk production assumed equal to infant suckling rate
